accessibility.accessibleNameSource: None needed: the content is the message.
announcements: role=alert (danger): assertive; announced when inserted with content or when its content changes

role=status (neutral): polite; only changes to a live region that already exists are reliably announced, so insert the empty sb-alert first and add the message afterwards, or render it with the page when it needs no announcement
aria: host role is set before the first render: status for feedback=neutral, alert for feedback=danger, and follows feedback while the author has not set a role
an authored role attribute is never overwritten
icon is decorative: authors mark it aria-hidden
sb-alert-title is a plain block, not a heading; use a real heading element inside it when the alert belongs in the document outline
data-has-icon and data-has-action are presentation-only host attributes set from slotchange
accessibility.role: status (feedback=neutral) or alert (feedback=danger); an explicit role attribute on the host wins
accessibility.targetSize: An action control inside follows its own component (at least 24px).

antiPatterns.alternative: Plain text, or feedback=neutral which is polite
antiPatterns.pattern: Using alert for every inline note
antiPatterns.why: Assertive live regions interrupt screen-reader users

antiPatterns.alternative: Insert it empty, then add the text
antiPatterns.pattern: Inserting a status alert already filled and expecting it to be announced
antiPatterns.why: Live regions announce changes to a region that already exists

Supporting text. Muted when neutral, in the alert color when danger.

openQuestions.answer: Default is role=status, destructive is role=alert; authored role wins.
openQuestions.question: role=alert for every variant (visual reference) or role=status for the default variant?
openQuestions.recommendation: status for default (polite), alert for destructive (assertive). An authored role wins. Document that live regions must exist before their content changes.

openQuestions.question: Title line-clamp-1 and the description's destructive/90 color?
openQuestions.recommendation: Drop both: truncating a title hides content (WCAG 1.4.10) and 90% destructive text risks 4.5:1.

feedback.note: neutral: card colors, announced politely (role=status). danger: error colors, announced assertively (role=alert).

contract.summary: A static message box for news people should notice without being interrupted: optional icon, title, description and action (a family of Web Components).

# Plan: Alert (planning gate)

Status: Approved under SB-0011 (owner pre-approval, 2026-11-08).

## Scope
`sb-alert` plus `sb-alert-title`, `sb-alert-description` and `sb-alert-action`, with feedback neutral and danger, an `icon` slot and an action area. Host role is `status` or `alert` by feedback.

## Files (in build order)
| Step | File |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `src/components/alert/Alert.stories.ts` |
| 2 | `playwright/tests/alert/alert.behavior.spec.ts` (written first, must fail) |
| 3 | `src/components/alert/Alert.scss` -> `Alert.styles.ts` (generated, shared by all parts) |
| 4 | `Alert.ts`, `AlertTitle.ts`, `AlertDescription.ts`, `AlertAction.ts`, `index.ts` |

## Tokens
`alert.*` aliases semantic tokens, including the new `space.stack.*`.

## Test plan (test-first)
- Role: status for neutral, alert for danger; present on an empty alert before content arrives and unchanged when content is added; follows `feedback`; authored role is kept.
- Layout: with an icon the content starts after 16px + 12px; without it, at the padding edge; action at the end.
- Colors per feedback (title and description) in light and dark; border, radius, padding.
- Title weight; no title truncation.
- axe clean on neutral, danger and action stories.

## Accessibility deviations from the references
- Role: `status` for neutral feedback (visual reference: `alert` always).
- No title line-clamp; description in full destructive color (not /90).

## Open questions
- Q1 Role alert vs status: answered, by variant, authored role wins.
- Q2 Title clamp and /90 tint: answered, dropped.
